title: The Progenitors after the Anomaly
summary: A support Convention in a fractured Union.

claims.text: Progenitors describe the Union after the Dimensional Anomaly as fractured and bleeding, with many colleagues wrongly declaring the Ascension War won.
They see themselves as a back-room support Convention supplying drugs, medical care, the odd sidekick and a great many clones.
Whispers in NWO halls speak of a brewing Technocratic civil war, made worse by the loss of the old alliances once kept in Horizon.

title: The Hippocratic Circle's long past
summary: Progenitor memory from the Renaissance to 1914.

claims.text: The Renaissance let healers leave the shadows the Church had forced them into, and doctors were welcome at courts everywhere.
Life-extension work let leading Technocrats live for centuries; Reginald Proctor, extended in 1715, was the only one lost before the Anomaly, by suicide in 1914.
Racism and sexism took hold in the Circle in the 1700s, demeaning its women and its non-European forebears, now called the Aesculapians.

title: Progenitor micro-Methodologies
summary: Small groups that fill gaps in the Convention.

claims.text: Fields such as veterinary medicine, farming and ecology fall outside the main Methodologies and are covered by small, lightly funded groups.
The Shalihotran Society, named for the first known veterinarian, fights animal diseases such as BSE, West Nile and SARS where economies depend on livestock.
The Agronomists bring together Progenitors versed in botany and agriculture.
FACADE Engineers make the clones used across every Convention and hold the keys to the long lives of nearly every Technocratic leader.
That gives them almost any resource they ask for, yet they rarely abuse it.
Their roots may lie in an Egyptian Cosian Circle around 300 AD that bred chimeras like the beast-headed gods of the Pharaohs.
The name stands for Forced Adaption and Clone Alteration Developmental Eugenicists.

title: Genegineers
summary: Designers of life at the genetic level.

claims.text: Genegineers build whole creatures from scratch in the genes instead of stitching together parts.
Their creations still suffer Rejection, so they build whole ecologies to sustain them rather than lock them away.
They trace their line to a Hippocratic Circle school founded by the Order of Reason in the 1300s, counting Galvani and Mendel among past Geniuses.

title: Pharmacopoeists
summary: The Progenitors' drug makers, a house divided.

claims.text: One side develops medicines from penicillin to vaccines and cancer treatments, along with small comforts such as hair growth aids.
The other runs street labs and illicit drug networks, a trade the Convention entered with good intentions but never kept clean.
They claim an unbroken line to Cosian Apothecaries of the 4th century BCE trained by Hippocrates.

title: Applied Sciences
summary: Progenitor field scientists and Damage Control.

claims.text: More than 90% of Progenitors fit the image of the lab researcher, but Applied Sciences go out to make the world better first-hand.
Its members, including Damage Control combat scientists, see themselves as a bridge between Progenitor science and the real world, not as hired muscle.
